articles.originalTitle: Further artists announced for Skulptur Projekte Münster 2027 - ArtReview
articles.title: Skulptur Projekte Münster 2027 Announces 13 Additional Artists and Groups
articles.excerpt: The sixth edition of Skulptur Projekte Münster has announced 13 additional artists and groups for site-specific commissions. Led by the curatorial collective What, How & for Whom, the exhibition will run from 13 June to 3 October.
articles.content: Following an initial announcement in June, Skulptur Projekte Münster has revealed 13 additional artists and groups contributing site-specific commissions to its sixth edition. Led by the curatorial collective What, How & for Whom (WHW), the exhibition will take place from 13 June to 3 October. The newly announced participants include Mercedes Azpilicueta, Nolan Oswald Dennis, Alice Creischer and Andreas Siekmann, Myvillages, Kosen Ohtsubo, Kapwani Kiwanga, Iman Issa, Natascha Sadr Haghighian, Ashfika Rahman, Vlatka Horvat, Anton Kats, Khalil Rabah, and Ali Cherri. In a statement, WHW noted that at a time when cancellations, censorship, and withdrawal have constrained cultural work, the project seeks to make room for voices to be heard and alternatives to be proposed. The collective stated that artworks in public spaces do not need to compete for visibility in an overly saturated world, but can instead offer time to witness and stay with what cannot readily be resolved. The exhibition hopes encounters with public art will allow misrepresented or obscured perspectives to be felt and acknowledged without forcing consensus.

articles.originalTitle: Sharjah Design Centre Unveils Plans for Rammed Earth Building Opening in 2029 - ArchDaily
articles.title: Sharjah Design Centre Scheduled to Open in 2029
articles.excerpt: Scheduled to open in 2029 in the United Arab Emirates, the Sharjah Design Centre will focus on material research, prototyping, and production.
articles.content: Scheduled to open in 2029, the Sharjah Design Centre will form part of the Sharjah Creative Quarter development in the United Arab Emirates. Designed by Taller de Arquitectura – Mauricio Rocha in collaboration with architect Daniel Rosselló, the institution will integrate specialist laboratories, research facilities, production spaces, and public programmes. Led by Sheikha Hind bint Majid Al Qasimi, the centre aims to connect designers, manufacturers, researchers, and entrepreneurs for material experimentation and knowledge exchange. The building incorporates rammed earth construction to respond to the local climate. Located across from University City, the facility will include seven specialist laboratories dedicated to textiles, rapid prototyping, glass, ceramics, jewellery, metal, and wood, alongside a Material Library and a Digital Archive. Research collaborations are already underway with Atelier LUMA and the American University of Sharjah. Through the Theatrum Al Kimiya initiative, the centre investigates locally sourced and waste-based materials, including salt, limestone, sand, clay, wool, and mycelium, building upon previous craft research publications.

articles.originalTitle: matteo thun transforms 72 apartments inside milan’s iconic brutalist torre velasca - Designboom
articles.title: Matteo Thun Transforms 72 Apartments Inside Milan's Iconic Torre Velasca
articles.excerpt: Matteo Thun & Partners has redesigned the interiors of 72 residences spanning floors 19 through 26 inside Milan's historic Torre Velasca. Set for a phased opening starting in fall 2026, the project combines preserved architectural elements with Italian design classics.
articles.content: Matteo Thun & Partners has completed the interior design for 72 residences and suites spanning floors 19 through 26 of the historic Torre Velasca in Milan. Originally designed by BBPR in 1958, the building is protected in collaboration with Italy's Ministry of Culture. During the renovation, kitchen and bathroom tiles, historic doors, window frames, and original loggias were preserved. Addressing low ceilings and compact rooms, the studio introduced glossy finishes that reflect daylight, alongside revised floor plans featuring larger showers and walk-in closets. In collaboration with Dedar, custom dusty pink wall coverings inspired by the building's exterior plaster were developed. This color is paired with mustard-yellow sofas custom-designed for Molteni and stone-finish coffee tables. Works by Italian designers including Gio Ponti, Afra and Tobia Scarpa, as well as pieces by Cassina and Oluce, are incorporated into the interiors. Forming part of a broader redevelopment led by Hines, the residences will operate under METT Milan Torre Velasca for short- and long-term stays, with a phased opening scheduled to begin in fall 2026.

articles.originalTitle: New research reveals original colours of Ancient Egyptian shrine at Oxford museum - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Ancient Egyptian Shrine at Oxford Museum Regains Original Colors Through Digital Projection
articles.excerpt: The nearly 3,000-year-old Shrine of King Taharqa at the Ashmolean Museum in Oxford is regaining its original colors through a digital projection based on research into surviving pigment traces.
articles.content: Housed at the Ashmolean Museum in Oxford, the Shrine of King Taharqa dating back to the pharaohs will be recolored through a digital projection starting 13 November. Built between 690 BC and 654 BC in northern Sudan, the monument features carvings and inscriptions analyzed through microscopic examination and hyperspectral imaging. According to Liam McNamara, the museum's keeper of antiquities, these methods revealed invisible traces of yellow and Egyptian blue alongside surviving red pigment in the sandstone crevices. The structure arrived in Oxford from Khartoum 90 years ago as a gift from the Sudanese government to excavation teams in Nubia. Supported by James Lupton and his wife Béatrice, the projection will allow visitors to view the original painted decoration for the first time within the Ancient Egypt and Sudan galleries.

articles.originalTitle: Has Time Been Unkind to Charles Ray’s Sculptures? - ArtReview
articles.title: Critical Perspectives on the Charles Ray Exhibition at the Fridericianum in Kassel
articles.excerpt: The Charles Ray exhibition at the Fridericianum in Kassel brings together the sculptor's works, material choices, and large-scale productions for viewers.
articles.content: The Charles Ray exhibition at Kassel's Fridericianum museum brings together a selection of sculptures spanning the artist's career. Among the works included in the exhibition is Oh! Charley, Charley, Charley… from 1992, a hand-painted fiberglass and synthetic hair installation featuring naked bodies. The presentation also features works such as Clothes Pile, created from aluminum and white paint, and Return to the One in papier-mâché. Earlier large-scale pieces like Firetruck, previously shown in New York, along with student-era photographs such as Plank Piece, offer context on the sculptor's trajectory. Figurative works including Aluminum Girl from 2003 and Boy with Frog from 2009 are also referenced as part of the artist's exploration of form and material. The exhibition provides visitors with an opportunity to examine the sculptor's decades-long material investigations and production processes.

articles.originalTitle: Another piece of King's Cross’ masterplan is complete – and is a fascinating example of prefab construction - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Cadence Residential Project Completed in London's King's Cross
articles.excerpt: Designed by Alison Brooks Architects in London's King's Cross, the Cadence residential complex has been completed using predominantly prefabricated components.
articles.content: Positioned at the northern edge of Lewis Cubitt Park in London's King's Cross, the Cadence residential complex has been completed. Designed by London-based architecture firm Alison Brooks Architects, the project comprises two towers of 12 and 16 storeys containing 163 residential units alongside commercial and social spaces. The design features a red brick facade paying homage to St Pancras station. Due to two underground Thameslink railway lines, the foundations required specialized structural isolators and precise alignment. Nearly 85 per cent of the building was constructed from prefabricated components manufactured off-site, including columns, beams, slabs, lift shafts, facade panels, and bathroom pods, installed in collaboration with contractor Laing O'Rourke. Construction experienced a three-month delay due to a protected redstart bird nesting on site. Of the 163 residential units, 60 affordable rentals were acquired for the CBRE UK Affordable Housing Fund, offering discounted market rents with priority given to Camden community residents, while market-rate homes were listed across various price tiers.

articles.originalTitle: Architect Kae Ito creates a modular ‘secret garden’ for Art Week Tokyo's bar - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Architect Kae Ito creates a modular secret garden for Art Week Tokyo
articles.excerpt: Japanese architect Kae Ito has created Kuru Kuru, a spatial design featuring modular and collapsible elements for the AWT Bar at Art Week Tokyo.
articles.content: Japanese architect Kae Ito has created Kuru Kuru, a spatial design for this year's AWT Bar at Art Week Tokyo. Having spent ten years at Sanaa before opening her independent firm in 2025, Ito drew inspiration from Mongolian traditional nomadic homes called ger to design modular and collapsible elements. The space features openwork structures of stainless steel and acrylic paired with color-coded acrylic hemispheres that function as seats or tables. The culinary experience is orchestrated by chef Ryuichi Yokomizo, who presents two deceptive canapés: a duck rillettes gâteau and a tarte tatin-inspired sablé. In addition, the menu includes inventive cocktails devised by artists Mariko Mori, Yoshihiro Suda, and Natsumi Aoyagi. Combining ambitious design, cuisine, and cocktails, the pop-up bar aims to provide visitors with a multisensory experience. The AWT Bar runs from 4 to 8 November during Art Week Tokyo.

articles.originalTitle: Foster + Partners and MANICA Unveil Design for New Stadium to Replace Milan's San Siro - ArchDaily
articles.title: Design Unveiled for Generali Stadium to Replace Milan's Historic San Siro
articles.excerpt: Designed by Foster + Partners and MANICA, the 71,500-seat Generali Stadium will be built alongside San Siro for AC Milan and Inter. Construction is expected in 2028, with estimated costs reaching approximately €1.2 billion.
articles.content: AC Milan and FC Internazionale Milano have unveiled the design for Generali Stadium, a 71,500-seat venue planned as the shared home for the two football clubs in Milan, Italy. Designed by Foster + Partners and MANICA, the new stadium will be built alongside the existing San Siro as part of a 281,000-square-meter surrounding area redevelopment. Construction is expected to begin in 2028, with the venue scheduled to host its first match during the 2031/32 season, subject to planning approvals. The design features a concrete X-frame structure supporting a roof equipped with 27,500 square meters of photovoltaic panels. Targeting LEED Gold certification, the facility is planned as an all-electric operation. The clubs estimate the construction cost at approximately €1.2 billion and have secured a naming-rights agreement with Generali valued at €650 million through 2052. San Siro is expected to remain operational until the new venue opens, after which most of its structure is planned for demolition.

articles.originalTitle: ArtReview Podcast Special | Andrew Maerkle – Art Week Tokyo - ArtReview
articles.title: ArtReview and Andrew Maerkle Discuss the Scope of Art Week Tokyo
articles.excerpt: Art Week Tokyo Editorial Director Andrew Maerkle speaks with ArtReview Editor-in-Chief Mark Rappolt regarding the origins of the initiative and contemporary art in Japan.
articles.content: Stating that contemporary art remains somewhat on the margins of culture in Japan, Art Week Tokyo Editorial Director Andrew Maerkle discusses ongoing efforts to engage new audiences. In a special podcast production in partnership with ArtReview, Maerkle speaks with Editor-in-Chief Mark Rappolt about the origins and impact of the initiative's programming. Organized by the Japan Contemporary Art Platform in collaboration with Art Basel and supported by Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, the annual showcase was founded in 2021 by gallerist Atsuko Ninagawa and collector Kazunari Shirai. The event runs from 4 to 8 November. As part of the partnership, ArtReview presents a panel featuring guest curators Maria Brewińska, Ekow Eshun, and Multiple Spirits, moderated by Mark Rappolt. The conversation takes place on Friday, 6 November, from 15:00 to 16:20 at the Sogetsu Kaikan venue in Akasaka, Minato-ku. Admission is free, and simultaneous interpretation in English and Japanese will be provided for attendees.

articles.originalTitle: ‘dismantling should be designed, not improvised’: THISS studio on radical reuse in architecture - Designboom
articles.title: THISS Studio Explores Radical Reuse and Design for Disassembly in Architecture
articles.excerpt: London-based THISS Studio rethinks the architectural design process and material life cycles through reclaimed components and structures designed for disassembly.
articles.content: London-based THISS Studio alters the traditional architectural design sequence by integrating reclaimed components and structures designed for disassembly into its projects. Founded by Tamsin Hanke and Sash Scott, the practice utilizes unlikely starting points such as an old barn, a pontoon boat, and dismantled exhibitions. The designers note that projects can no longer be fully resolved on paper before gathering stock and making adjustments during construction. For Barn Again at the 2025 Copenhagen Architecture Biennial, beams recovered from disused barns formed a tapering pavilion designed for disassembly. At Kiko Kostadinov's London flagship, inverted railings became a ceiling-mounted support system for shelving. In Cairo, the Pergola outdoor theater incorporated materials from local reuse initiatives. For exhibition designs, the studio employs all-timber assemblies without metal fixings and conducts inventory assessments to preserve components for subsequent use. The founders emphasize that institutions must adapt their funding and procurement schedules to accommodate reclaimed stock, arguing that dismantling must be deliberately designed rather than improvised.

articles.originalTitle: herzog & de meuron to convert former birkenstock warehouse into the eames institute museum - Designboom
articles.title: Herzog & de Meuron to Convert Former California Campus Into Eames Institute Museum
articles.excerpt: Herzog & de Meuron has revealed plans to convert a former campus in Novato, California, into the future museum of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity. Spanning approximately 88 acres, the project is targeting an opening in 2030.
articles.content: Spanning approximately 88 acres in Novato, California, a former campus previously associated with McGraw-Hill and Birkenstock is being converted into the museum of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity by Herzog & de Meuron. Featuring San Francisco practice EHDD as executive architect and landscape design by Field Operations, the master plan has been submitted to the City of Novato. The campus's most prominent element is its roof, formed from hyperbolic paraboloid shells designed by Jan Lubicz-Nycz and developed with engineer Raj Desai. The proposal organizes interiors around a central hall keeping the roof geometry visible, incorporating exhibition spaces, workshops, a theater, and a steel-clad reflective bridge. Recessed glass facades at the northern and southern edges connect interiors with gardens, while Field Operations links 10 gardens through pathways featuring native plant species. Following the Institute's property acquisition, major construction is intended to begin in 2028, with an opening targeted for 2030.

articles.originalTitle: Drop-in Design: Your Future City - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Designing the Future City Workshop at the V&A Museum
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum invites families and children aged 5 and over to design future public buildings using recycled materials in a free workshop.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a hands-on town planning event for children and families in collaboration with architectural designer Jahba Anan and RIBA. At the V&A South Kensington, participants will imagine and redesign how schools, hospitals, libraries, and train stations might look in 2050. Drawing inspiration from the Design 1900–Now galleries, the program allows visitors to examine how design has transformed daily life over the past 125 years. Supported by the Adobe Foundation, attendees will use recycled materials to build mini models of their dream buildings and contribute them to a growing city model over five days. The free drop-in event is suitable for ages 5 and above, with all materials provided on-site. Visitors must ensure children are attended at all times. The venue offers comprehensive accessibility features, including baby-changing facilities, quiet spaces, and ear defenders available upon request from the Learning Centre Desk for families requiring sensory support.

articles.originalTitle: Human Unreadable Act III by Operator - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Operator Duo Livestreams Act Three of Human Unreadable at the V&A
articles.excerpt: Artist duo Operator brings the final act of their Human Unreadable series, examining human and machine agency, to the Victoria and Albert Museum.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a livestream screening of Act III, the final act of the three-part work Human Unreadable by artist duo Operator, on 22 November 2026. Transmitted live from the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York, the multimedia performance examines negotiations between the body, ambition, and technology. The presentation utilizes 100 dance sequences from the Human Unreadable collection, woven together through scripted dialogue, performance art, lighting, scenic design, and an original score. Broadcast across multiple venues, the transmission features real-time editing from multiple camera perspectives. Commissioned by the Whitney Museum of American Art, the event forms part of the museum's digital art season exploring boundaries between human and machine agency.

articles.originalTitle: Marsden Hartley | Painting No. 50 | L1396 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Marsden Hartley's Painting No. 50 Reflects His Berlin Years
articles.excerpt: Created in Berlin between 1914 and 1915 by US artist Marsden Hartley, Painting No. 50 blends Native American cultural references with German military pageantry.
articles.content: Painting No. 50, a striking work by US artist Marsden Hartley created as part of his Amerika series after moving to Berlin in 1913, is on display at the National Gallery. Influenced by the militaristic atmosphere of pre-First World War Berlin, the artist integrated the choreography of street parades into his visual vocabulary. At the center of the composition, Hartley stacked simplified elements such as a teepee, a canoe, and a bow and arrow, incorporating black and yellow zigzags reminiscent of military insignia alongside concentric target-like circles. Although he had no direct contact with Native American communities while living in the United States, Hartley drew inspiration from popular culture and ethnographic museum collections in Paris and Berlin. This synthesis allowed him to align with the European avant-garde while simultaneously crafting a distinct American identity for European audiences. Due to wartime travel restrictions and rising hostility toward immigrants, Hartley returned to his home country in 1915. The oil on canvas composition is on loan from the Terra Foundation for American Art and is exhibited in Room 45.

articles.originalTitle: HISTORICAL ARCHIVE | The Pillar and Ground of the Truth by Pavel A. Florenskij - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale Stages Pavel A. Florensky Project at Historical Archive
articles.excerpt: The Historical Archive of La Biennale di Venezia will present a five-day special project dedicated to Pavel A. Florensky, exploring the relationship between language and truth. The performances will take place from 16 to 20 November at the Arsenale.
articles.content: La Biennale di Venezia is presenting The Pillar and Ground of the Truth by Pavel A. Florensky as part of the Biennale of the Word. Taking place from 16 to 20 November 2026 at the new premises of the Historical Archive at the Arsenale, the project is conceived and directed by Antonello Pocetti across five evenings. The texts have been adapted from Florensky's writings to convey the depth of his reflections. Each evening opens with contributions from figures in culture, philosophy, and religion, followed by staged readings. Born in 1882 in Yevlakh, Azerbaijan, Florensky studied mathematics in Moscow before turning to philosophy and theology. Ordained an Orthodox priest in 1911, he engaged in research spanning mathematics, music, painting, and philosophy. Following the 1917 Revolution, he remained in Russia, where he participated in scientific projects before being arrested on counter-revolutionary charges and executed near Leningrad on 8 December 1937. Tickets become available starting 29 October on the La Biennale di Venezia website.

articles.originalTitle: Unboxing Victorian mourning: dress, human hair jewellery and postmortem photos - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Unboxes 19th Century Victorian Mourning Traditions
articles.excerpt: Victoria and Albert Museum curators released a video exploring 19th century mourning traditions, featuring human hair jewellery and postmortem photography.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum released a video examining 19th century mourning traditions. Curators Ruth and Lydia presented a genuine Victorian mourning outfit, intricate jewellery crafted from human hair, and postmortem photographs used to memorialise the deceased. The presentation highlights how grief, love, and art intertwined during the 19th century through jet jewellery, veils, and specific mourning cards. The video also explores the practice of Victorian postmortem photography, wherein families captured their final memories with departed loved ones. The institution utilizes third-party platforms to share content on its website, requiring user consent for targeting cookies. This digital release forms part of the museum's ongoing efforts to document and share its extensive collections and historical research with a wider public audience through online channels.

articles.originalTitle: Michele Bönan Has Been Designing Hotels for Over 50 Years. And Is Still at the Top of His Game - WWD
articles.title: Italian Architect Michele Bönan Marks Over 50 Years of Luxury Hotel Design
articles.excerpt: With a career spanning nearly 50 years, Florence-based architect Michele Bönan is known for blending Italian craftsmanship, contemporary art, and antiques in luxury hotel and residential projects.
articles.content: Florence-based architect Michele Bönan has spent over 50 years shaping luxury hospitality with an aesthetic that combines Italian craftsmanship, contemporary art, antiques, and bespoke furnishings. His portfolio features prominent names such as Rocco Forte Hotels, the Lungarno Collection, Casa Cipriani, and J.K. Place. Bönan observes that the definition of luxury has evolved toward wellness, privacy, and a sense of belonging rather than impersonal grandeur. His career took off in the 1980s following the publication of his work on a Forte dei Marmi estate. More recently, his projects include the May opening of Casa J.K. Place Roma, featuring 12 residences inside an 18th-century Roman palazzo outfitted with custom details, statuario marble floors, and historic fireplaces. In 2021, he launched the Michele Bonan Interiors collection alongside his son Sky Bonan. Looking ahead, Bönan is currently transforming the historic Palazzo dei Principi Caravita di Sirignano in Naples into a property slated to open in 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Bernard Arnault on Craftsmanship, Creativity and Passion [PHOTOS] - WWD
articles.title: Photographs Highlighting Bernard Arnault and His Dedication to Craftsmanship
articles.excerpt: Archival photographs trace Bernard Arnault's life journey from childhood and early family business involvement to his education at École Polytechnique and visits to LVMH ateliers.
articles.content: A series of archival photographs documents the life and career trajectory of Bernard Arnault, focusing on his enduring connection to craftsmanship. The collection features early portraits, including Arnault with his mother Marie Josèphe Savinel in 1950, with his sister Dominique in 1953, and with his parents in 1958. Additional images capture him alongside his grandfather at the family company around 1959, with his grandmother Elisa Jeanne Gachon in 1967, and during his studies at École Polytechnique in 1969. Later photographs document professional milestones, such as his collaborations and appearances with architect Frank Gehry in front of the Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris and visits to the Institut de France de Paris. The visual record concludes with interior views of ateliers across various luxury houses, including Berluti, Chaumet, Tiffany, and Bvlgari, capturing craftsmanship activities during the Journées Particulières LVMH 2026 events.

articles.originalTitle: Unique collection of historic Anglo-Indian artworks gifted to Tate by Charles Greig – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Receives Collection of 50 Anglo-Indian Artworks Donated by Charles Greig
articles.excerpt: Art historian Charles Greig has donated 50 artworks depicting 18th and 19th-century India to Tate. Comprising oil paintings, watercolours, and miniatures, the collection will debut at Tate Britain in 2028.
articles.content: Tate has acquired a collection of 50 artworks donated by art historian Charles Greig. Gifted outright without tax incentives, the donation features pieces created by artists who lived and worked in India during the 18th and 19th centuries. Assembled by Greig over four decades, the collection comprises oil paintings, watercolours, and miniatures reflecting South Asian visual culture. The works include pieces by Indian artists Sita Ram and Ghulam Ali Khan, European creators Johan Zoffany and Rudolf Swoboda, and British landscapists William Hodges, Thomas Daniell, and William Daniell. Key highlights feature Johan Zoffany's 1784 Portrait of Prince Jawan Bakht, marking one of only three portraits of individual Indian sitters by the artist held in UK public collections. Another notable work is Rudolph Swoboda's portrait of a sepoy from Srinagar's Indian regiment. The public will be able to view the collection for the first time in 2028 during a dedicated free display at Tate Britain. Tate Britain Director Alex Farquharson stated that the exceptional gift significantly strengthens the institution's holdings of art produced within the British Empire. Greig expressed profound happiness that the works have found a permanent home at Tate to remain universally accessible.

articles.originalTitle: EXCLUSIVE: DeMellier Opens Its First Store in London’s Sloane Square, Designed to Feel Like a Stylish Home - WWD
articles.title: Luxury Handbag Brand DeMellier Opens First Store in London's Sloane Square
articles.excerpt: Approaching its 10th anniversary, luxury handbag brand DeMellier has opened its first stand-alone store in London's Sloane Square, designed to evoke a warm, residential atmosphere.
articles.content: Approaching its 10th anniversary, luxury handbag brand DeMellier has opened its inaugural stand-alone store in London's Sloane Square. Founder Mireia Llusia-Lindh collaborated with residential architect Nicolas Schuybroek to fashion a 3,230-square-foot space across two floors that mimics a stylish home rather than a traditional retail environment. The ground floor resembles a living room where handbags are displayed on marble shelves, while the lower level features a dining table format and a craft corner displaying leather-cutting tools, needles, and artisan films. The interior incorporates oak floors, mineral plaster walls, and abstract paintings by British artist Susan Gunn. Operating primarily as an online business that accounts for 80 percent of its sales, the profitable company closed its financial year with 56 million pounds in revenue. DeMellier employs responsibly sourced leather and contributes a portion of every sale to SOS Children’s Villages through its philanthropic initiative to support children in need.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | RAW Material Company - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: RAW Material Company Presents Educational Framework at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Shaped by the vision of late founder Koyo Kouoh, RAW Material Company highlights collective knowledge production and anti-hierarchical structures in its Biennale Arte 2026 presentation.
articles.content: Established to make the knowledge of the people a central pillar in serving society, RAW Material Company engages in curatorial practice, artistic education, residencies, and knowledge archiving. Informed by literature, film, architecture, politics, fashion, and cuisine, its trans-disciplinary program fosters creative growth in Africa while anchored in Dakar. Conceived by its late founder and artistic director, Koyo Kouoh, as an educational space distinct from traditional degree-granting institutions, it operates as a school of life where artists, lawyers, activists, students, architects, and chefs gather. Operating with an all-female team since its inception, the organization places people at the center of its infrastructure. The presentation at Biennale Arte 2026, titled Ideal Seeds for Fertile Grounds, reflects an approach where long-term relationships with practitioners support pedagogy through the open circulation of ideas, recognizing that knowledge remains inherently collective.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Nairobi Contemporary Art Institute (NCAI) - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Nairobi Contemporary Art Institute Features East African Works at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: The Nairobi Contemporary Art Institute presents a selection of 8 paintings created between 1950 and 1984 by artists trained at Makerere University at the Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Founded in 2020, the Nairobi Contemporary Art Institute works to preserve, promote, and make contemporary art freely available across East Africa. Despite the vitality of regional artistic production, many significant works have left East Africa, acquired by collectors and institutions in Europe and North America. The institute has built its permanent collection in response to recover works as records of an artistic culture. On view at the Biennale Arte 2026 are 8 paintings created between 1950 and 1984 by artists who trained at Makerere University in Kampala, Uganda. These include works by Sam Joseph Nitro, a diplomat who built Tanzania's first arts faculty, and painter Josephine Alacu, who transformed political trauma into allegory. These figures demonstrate why Makerere's legacy holds a central place in East Africa's artistic history.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Beverly Buchanan - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Beverly Buchanan's Artistic Legacy Featured at the Venice Biennale
articles.excerpt: The Beverly Buchanan presentation at the 2026 Venice Biennale brings together drawings, paintings, sculptures, and earthworks to examine Black Southern building traditions.
articles.content: The Biennale Arte 2026 highlights the multidisciplinary practice of American artist Beverly Buchanan, spanning drawings, paintings, sculptures, and earthworks. Raised in South Carolina and educated at Columbia University, Buchanan exhibited in New York before returning to the American South in 1977. Her presentation emphasizes her self-reflexive voice through field work, research notes, and accompanying texts known as legends. Utilizing diverse materials ranging from thrifted timbers and metals to medical spatulas and bottle caps, Buchanan's shack sculptures commemorate Black cultural preservation and the creative ingenuity of self-taught architects and artists such as Mary Lou Furcron and Nellie Mae Rowe. Her concrete and tabby works engage with the vulnerabilities of building materials exposed to natural elements and tidal salt water along coastal regions.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Issa Samb - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Biennale Arte 2026 Features the Artistic Legacy of Issa Samb
articles.excerpt: The works of Senegalese artist Issa Samb are presented at the Central Pavilion and Arsenale during Biennale Arte 2026. The exhibition features installations inspired by his Dakar courtyard and documentary contributions.
articles.content: Senegalese artist Issa Samb, who lived from 1945 to 2017 in Dakar, is commemorated through installations displayed at the Central Pavilion and Arsenale during Biennale Arte 2026. Hailing from the Lebou community and also known as Joe Ouakam, Samb worked across painting, collage, assemblage, sculpture, performance, and writing. His home and courtyard in Dakar, La Cour, served for many years as a crossroads for artistic and political thought. As a co-founder of the Laboratoire Agit’Art collective alongside Djibril Diop Mambéty, Samb maintained that artworks should be experienced and touched by the public. Known for destroying and recreating his works as a means of transformation, his presence in the Biennale consists of installations featuring costumes, suspended objects, notes, and sketches. The presentation also includes a video contribution by Adrienne Edwards documenting a visit to La Cour, alongside Ican Ramageli's film Cap Vers l’Est. Visitors can view the exhibition at the Central Pavilion and Arsenale.

articles.originalTitle: Obama Presidential Center Reaches $1B in Total Costs - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Obama Presidential Center Reaches $1 Billion in Total Costs
articles.excerpt: The total cost of the Barack Obama Presidential Center in Chicago has reached approximately $1 billion, compared to its original $350 million budget.
articles.content: The campus cost of the Barack Obama Presidential Center on Chicago's South Side has reached $1 billion. According to the latest filing from the non-profit Obama Foundation, this latest figure is about $91 million above the September projection of $909 million, excluding $123 million in publicly financed infrastructure improvements. Emily Bittner, the foundation's vice president of communications, stated that the costs are raised through private contributions. The foundation stated it has no outstanding disputed charges with Lakeside Alliance, the joint venture contractor that completed the main building. The project's budget was originally announced as $350 million, jumped to $500 million when design was completed in 2017, and reached $850 million in early September before the latest filing. The recent increases were attributed to additional construction scope such as the Home Court basketball center, public art, and insurance.
